section.content: The invention provides a lithium ion battery. The lithium ion battery includes a battery case, an electrolyte, and an electrode assembly. The electrolyte comprises lithium salt and an organic solvent, and the electrode assembly comprises a positive plate, a negative plate and an isolating membrane. The positive plate comprises a positive current collector and a positive membrane which is arranged on at least one surface of the positive current collector and comprises a positive active material, and the negative plate comprises a negative current collector and a negative membrane which is arranged on at least one surface of the negative current collector and comprises a negative active material. The lithium salt comprises one or more compounds shown as a formula I, wherein n is an integer from 1 to 3, and Rf1And Rf2Is CmF2m+1Wherein m is an integer of 0 to 5, Rf1、Rf2The lithium ion batteries are the same or different, and the group margin of the lithium ion batteries is 85-95%. The lithium ion battery has the advantages of good cycle performance, good rate performance, high safety performance and good low-temperature discharge performance.

本发明提供一种锂离子电池。所述锂离子电池包括电池壳体、电解液以及电极组件。所述电解液包括锂盐以及有机溶剂，所述电极组件由正极片、负极片以及隔离膜组成。所述正极片包括正极集流体以及设置于正极集流体至少一个表面上且包括正极活性材料的正极膜片，所述负极片包括负极集流体以及设置于负极集流体至少一个表面上且包括负极活性材料的负极膜片。所述锂盐包括式I所示的化合物中的一种或几种，其中，n为1～3内的整数，Rf1和Rf2是CmF2m+1，其中m为0～5内的整数，Rf1、Rf2相同或不同，所述锂离子电池的群裕度为85％～95％。本发明的锂离子电池具有循环性能好、倍率性能好、安全性能高、低温放电性能好的优点。

Lithium ion batteryTechnical Field

The invention relates to the technical field of batteries, in particular to a lithium ion battery.

Background

Lithium ion batteries are widely used in electric vehicles and consumer electronics because of their advantages of high energy density, high output power, long cycle life, and low environmental pollution. The demand in the market today for lithium ion batteries is both a requirement for their advantages of high power, long cycle life and long storage life, and a requirement for their high energy density.

With the development of miniaturization and weight reduction of lithium ion batteries, the demand for energy density is higher and higher. At present, in the prior art, in order to improve the energy density of a lithium ion battery, the following solutions are generally adopted: active materials in the electrode are compacted as much as possible, so that the battery can contain more electrode active materials on the premise of not changing the volume occupied space of the battery, for example, the coating weight of a pole piece is higher and higher, and the group margin design is larger and larger, so that the charging power performance and the discharging power performance of the lithium ion battery are deteriorated, the cycle life performance is not good, and the like. Therefore, it is desirable to provide a lithium ion battery with high energy density, low impedance, good dynamic performance and high safety factor.

Disclosure of Invention

In view of the problems in the background art, an object of the present invention is to provide a lithium ion battery, which has the advantages of high energy density, good cycle performance, and good rate performance, and also has good low-temperature discharge performance and safety performance.

In order to achieve the above object, the present invention provides a lithium ion battery including a battery case, an electrolyte, and an electrode assembly. The electrolyte comprises lithium salt and an organic solvent, and the electrode assembly comprises a positive plate, a negative plate and an isolating membrane. The positive plate comprises a positive current collector and a positive membrane which is arranged on at least one surface of the positive current collector and comprises a positive active material, and the negative plate comprises a negative current collector and a negative membrane which is arranged on at least one surface of the negative current collector and comprises a negative active material. The lithium salt comprises one or more compounds shown as a formula I, wherein n is an integer from 1 to 3, and Rf1And Rf2Is CmF2m+1Wherein m is an integer of 0 to 5, Rf1、Rf2The lithium ion batteries are the same or different, and the group margin of the lithium ion batteries is 85-95%.

The invention at least comprises the following beneficial effects:

the lithium ion battery comprises one or more imine lithium salts shown in formula I, and has the advantages of good cycle performance, good rate performance, high safety performance and good low-temperature discharge performance.

The lithium ion battery of the invention has the advantage of high energy density by adjusting the group margin of the lithium ion battery on the basis of using the imine type lithium salt shown in the formula I.

Detailed Description

The lithium ion battery according to the present invention is explained in detail below.

The lithium ion battery of the present invention includes a battery case, an electrolyte, and an electrode assembly. The electrolyte comprises lithium salt and an organic solvent, and the electrode assembly comprises a positive plate, a negative plate and an isolating membrane. The positive plate comprises a positive current collector and a positive membrane which is arranged on at least one surface of the positive current collector and comprises a positive active material, and the negative plate comprises a negative current collector and a negative membrane which is arranged on at least one surface of the negative current collector and comprises a negative active material. The lithium salt comprises one or more compounds shown as a formula I, wherein n is an integer from 1 to 3, and Rf1And Rf2Is CmF2m+1Wherein m is an integer of 0 to 5, Rf1、Rf2The lithium ion batteries are the same or different, and the group margin of the lithium ion batteries is 85-95%.

The group margin of the lithium ion battery is 85-95%. The group margin is the ratio of the actual internal sectional area to the maximum internal sectional area of the lithium ion battery, namely the filling rate, and can represent the difficulty degree of the electrode assembly entering the shell, the pressure of the electrode assembly on the battery shell after charging and expanding, and the like.

There are two ways to calculate the group margin, which are:

(1) group margin is the whole sectional area of the electrode assembly/the internal space area of the battery shell;

(2) group margin is electrode assembly thickness/cell case internal thickness.

The smaller the group margin of the lithium ion battery, the easier the electrode assembly is to be housed, but the lithium ion battery with the small group margin also has a relatively low energy density, and thus may not meet practical use requirements. The larger the group margin of the lithium ion battery is, the more difficult the electrode assembly is to enter the shell, so that the process difficulty is increased, and the electrode assembly is damaged; the lithium ion battery with large group margin has relatively less electrolyte occupation ratio, so that the cycle performance and the rate performance of the lithium ion battery can be influenced; in addition, in the lithium ion battery having a large group margin, since the pressure of the battery case is increased after the electrode assembly is charged and expanded, the safety performance of the lithium ion battery is deteriorated. The group margin of the lithium ion battery is 85-95%, and the lithium ion battery has high energy density and does not deteriorate the cycle performance, rate capability and safety performance of the lithium ion battery.

Currently common lithium ion batteries use conventional lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF)6) As a lithium salt, due to LiPF6The lithium ion battery is easy to decompose at high temperature and extremely sensitive to moisture, and cannot be applied to a special environment with high energy density, and the lithium ion battery usually has the problems of poor rate capability, poor cycle performance, poor safety performance and the like, so that the actual use requirement is difficult to meet. The lithium ion battery electrolyte disclosed by the invention comprises the imine lithium salt in the formula I, so that the cycle performance, the rate capability and the safety performance of the lithium ion battery can be obviously improved, and the low-temperature discharge performance of the lithium ion battery can be improved. The reason is that the thermal decomposition temperature of the imine lithium salt in the formula I is usually more than 200 ℃, so that the imine lithium salt has the advantage of good thermal stability, and meanwhile, the imine lithium salt in the formula I can normally work in an environment of lower than-20 ℃; the imine lithium salt of the formula I also has excellent conductivity, Li+Has low binding energy with imine anion, Li+The dissociation degree is high, so that the electrolyte has higher conductivity; the imine lithium salt in the formula I is also beneficial to reducing the film forming impedance of the surfaces of the positive electrode and the negative electrode and forming a stable interface protective film with good ion conductivity on the surfaces of the positive electrode and the negative electrode.

However, if the content of the imine type lithium salt in formula I in the electrolyte is too low, the electrolyte is too lowMiddle Li+The content of the electrolyte is low, and the conductivity of the electrolyte is not obviously improved, so that the cycle performance and the rate performance of the lithium ion battery are not obviously improved; if the content of the imine lithium salt in the formula I in the electrolyte is too high, the viscosity of the electrolyte is excessively increased, which is not favorable for improving the cycle performance and low-temperature discharge performance of the lithium ion battery. In the lithium ion battery, the mass of the imine lithium salt in the formula I is 5-25% of the total mass of the electrolyte, and the cycle performance, the rate capability and the low-temperature discharge performance of the lithium ion battery can be improved simultaneously within the range.

In the lithium ion battery provided by the invention, although the lithium ion battery can have good safety performance, the problem of general nail penetration safety performance still exists, especially for the lithium ion battery with higher energy density. The through-nail safety performance of the lithium ion battery is closely related to the performance of the positive current collector, the smaller the thickness of the positive current collector is, the smaller the metal burr formed on the positive current collector after through-nail is, and the better the through-nail safety performance of the lithium ion battery is, but if the thickness of the positive current collector is too small, the risk of belt breakage may occur in the production process of the positive plate, so that the production cannot be smoothly carried out. Preferably, the thickness of the positive electrode current collector is 5 to 20 μm.

In the lithium ion battery, the fracture elongation of the positive electrode current collector also influences the nail penetration safety performance of the lithium ion battery. The larger the fracture elongation of the positive current collector is, the larger the metal burr formed on the positive current collector after nailing is, and meanwhile, the larger burr may be formed after the imine lithium salt in the formula I corrodes the positive current collector, so that the nailing safety performance of the lithium ion battery is not improved; however, if the elongation at break of the positive electrode current collector is too small, the ductility of the positive electrode current collector is difficult to meet the requirement of processing, and therefore, the positive electrode current collector is not favorable for processing and production of the positive electrode sheet. Preferably, the elongation at break of the positive electrode current collector is 0.8% to 4%.

In the lithium ion battery of the present invention, preferably, the positive electrode current collector is selected from aluminum foils. Because the imine lithium salt in the formula I can corrode the aluminum foil to a certain extent, aluminum oxide layers can be arranged on two surfaces of the aluminum foil so as to reduce the corrosion effect of the imine lithium salt in the formula I on the aluminum foil. Preferably, the thickness of the aluminum oxide layer is 5nm to 40 nm.

In the lithium ion battery of the invention, because the imine lithium salt in the formula I can corrode the anode current collector, a proper amount of lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF) can be added into the electrolyte6) So as to relieve the corrosion effect of the imine type lithium salt in the formula I on the positive electrode current collector. But LiPF6Should not be added in too large an amount due to LiPF6Gases such as HF are easily decomposed at high temperatures, and the generated gases not only corrode a positive electrode active material but also deteriorate the safety performance of a lithium ion battery. Preferably, LiFP6The mass of (a) is 0-10% of the total mass of the electrolyte.

In the lithium ion battery, the coating weight of the positive plate can also influence the energy density of the lithium ion battery, wherein the energy density of the lithium ion battery is improved more obviously when the coating weight of the positive plate is larger. However, the application weight of the positive electrode sheet is too large, which is not favorable for the cycle performance and rate performance of the lithium ion battery, and the coating weight of the positive electrode sheet is too large, which tends to cause lithium precipitation inside the battery, thereby deteriorating the performance of the lithium ion battery. Preferably, the single-side coating weight of the positive plate is 0.015g/cm2～0.023g/cm2。

In the lithium ion battery according to the second aspect of the present invention, the positive electrode active material is selected from materials capable of extracting and intercalating lithium ions. Specifically, the positive electrode active material may be selected from one or more of lithium cobalt oxide, lithium nickel oxide, lithium manganese oxide, lithium nickel cobalt aluminum oxide, and compounds obtained by adding other transition metals or non-transition metals to the above compounds, but the present invention is not limited to these materials.

In the lithium ion battery of the present invention, the positive electrode membrane may further include a conductive agent and a binder, where the types and contents of the conductive agent and the binder are not particularly limited and may be selected according to actual requirements.

In the lithium ion battery of the present invention, the negative electrode sheet may include a negative electrode current collector and a negative electrode membrane disposed on the negative electrode current collector and including a negative electrode active material, and the negative electrode membrane may be disposed on one surface of the negative electrode current collector or may be disposed on both surfaces of the negative electrode current collector. The kind of the negative electrode active material is not particularly limited, and may be preferably selected from one or more of graphite, soft carbon, hard carbon, mesocarbon microbeads, carbon fibers, carbon nanotubes, elemental silicon, silica compounds, silicon-carbon composites, silicon alloys, elemental tin, tin oxide compounds, and lithium titanate. The negative electrode diaphragm can also comprise a conductive agent and a binder, wherein the types and the contents of the conductive agent and the binder are not particularly limited and can be selected according to actual requirements. The type of the negative current collector is not particularly limited, and can be selected according to actual requirements.

In the lithium ion battery of the present invention, the negative electrode sheet may also be metallic lithium or a lithium alloy.

In the lithium ion battery, the isolation film is arranged between the positive plate and the negative plate and plays a role in isolation. The kind of the separator is not particularly limited, and may be any separator material used in the existing battery, such as polyethylene, polypropylene, polyvinylidene fluoride, and multi-layer composite films thereof, but is not limited thereto.

In the lithium ion battery of the present invention, the organic solvent may further include one or more of other kinds of chain carbonates, cyclic carbonates, and carboxylic esters. Among them, the kinds of the chain carbonate, the cyclic carbonate, and the carboxylic ester are not particularly limited, and may be selected according to actual needs. Preferably, the organic solvent may further include one or more of diethyl carbonate, dipropyl carbonate, ethyl methyl carbonate, propyl ethyl carbonate, ethylene carbonate, propylene carbonate, butylene carbonate, gamma-butyrolactone, methyl formate, ethyl acetate, propyl acetate, methyl propionate, ethyl propionate, methyl propionate, and tetrahydrofuran.

In the lithium ion battery according to the present invention, the mass of the cyclic carbonate is preferably 10% or less of the total mass of the electrolyte solution. Preferably, the cyclic carbonate may include Ethylene Carbonate (EC). Ethylene carbonate is easy to oxidize and generates a large amount of gas, which poses a certain threat to the safety of the lithium ion battery, but the ethylene carbonate has higher dielectric constant, and the conventional LiPF has6The system, if its content is reduced, has a great influence on the conductivity. On the other hand, based on the imine lithium salt in the formula I, the electrolyte still has good conductivity at low EC content because the anion and cation forces of the lithium salt are small. In the lithium ion battery according to the present invention, the lithium ion battery case is preferably a hard case made of a metal material.

In the lithium ion battery provided by the invention, in the lithium ion batteries with the same shell size, the larger the energy density of the lithium ion battery is, the more easily the exertion of the corresponding cycle performance, rate capability and safety performance is influenced, and the use of the imine type lithium salt including I can achieve the purpose of improving the cycle performance, rate capability and safety performance on the basis of keeping the high energy density of the lithium ion battery, thereby meeting the actual use requirement. The lithium ion battery provided by the invention has the advantages that the good cycle performance, the rate capability and the safety performance are considered on the basis of keeping the capacity not less than 150 Ah.

The invention is further illustrated by the following examples. It should be understood that these examples are for illustrative purposes only and are not intended to limit the scope of the present invention.

The lithium ion batteries of examples 1 to 28 and comparative examples 1 to 9 were each prepared as follows

(1) Preparation of positive plate

LiNi serving as a positive electrode active material0.5Mn0.3Co0.2O2Dissolving acetylene black serving as a conductive agent and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) serving as a binder in a solvent N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) according to a weight ratio of 94:3:3, and fully stirring and uniformly mixing to obtain anode slurry; then evenly coating the positive electrode slurry on a positive electrode current collector, and then drying, cold-pressing and cutting to obtain a positive electrode plate, wherein,the parameters of the positive electrode current collector and the coating weight of the positive electrode sheet are shown in table 1.

(2) Preparation of negative plate

Dissolving active substance artificial graphite, conductive agent acetylene black, binder Styrene Butadiene Rubber (SBR) and thickener carboxymethylcellulose sodium (CMC) in solvent deionized water according to a weight ratio of 95:2:2:1, and uniformly mixing with the solvent deionized water to prepare cathode slurry; and then uniformly coating the negative electrode slurry on a copper foil of a negative current collector, drying to obtain a negative electrode diaphragm, and performing cold pressing and slitting to obtain the negative electrode sheet.

(3) Preparation of the electrolyte

In an argon atmosphere glove box (H)2O<0.1ppm，O2<0.1ppm), the organic solvents shown in table 2 were mixed in a ratio, and then the lithium salt fully dried shown in table 2 was dissolved in the organic solvent to obtain an electrolytic solution.

(4) Preparation of the separator

A conventional polypropylene film was used as the separator.

(5) Preparation of lithium ion battery

Stacking the positive plate, the isolating film and the negative plate in sequence to enable the isolating film to be positioned between the positive plate and the negative plate to play an isolating role, and then winding to obtain an electrode assembly; and placing the electrode assembly in a battery shell, drying, injecting electrolyte, and preparing the lithium ion battery by processes of formation, standing and the like. The group margin of the lithium ion battery is shown in table 3. The method for testing the lithium ion battery group margin comprises the following steps: the internal thickness of the test square lithium ion battery shell is recorded as L1, the thickness of the test electrode assembly is recorded as L2, and the lithium ion battery group margin is L2/L1.

Next, a test procedure of the lithium ion battery is explained.

(1) Rate capability test of lithium ion battery

At 25 ℃, the lithium ion battery was charged to 4.3V at a constant current of 0.5C, then charged at a constant voltage of 4.3V to a current of less than 0.05C, and then discharged to 2.8V at a constant current of 0.5C, resulting in a discharge capacity at 0.5C.

At 25 ℃, the lithium ion battery was charged to 4.3V at a constant current of 0.5C, then charged at a constant voltage of 4.3V to a current of less than 0.05C, and then discharged to 2.8V at a constant current of 2C, resulting in a discharge capacity at 2C.

Lithium ion battery 2C/0.5C rate performance (%) — (discharge capacity at 2C/discharge capacity at 0.5C) × 100%.

(2) Cycle performance testing of lithium ion batteries

At 25 ℃, the lithium ion battery is charged to 4.3V at a constant current of 1C, then charged to a current of less than 0.05C at a constant voltage of 4.3V, and then discharged to 2.8V at a constant current of 1C, which is a charging and discharging process. The charge and discharge were repeated in this manner, and the capacity retention rate after 1000 cycles of the lithium ion battery was calculated.

Capacity retention (%) of the lithium ion battery after 1000 cycles at 25 ℃ ═ 100% of (discharge capacity at 1000 th cycle/discharge capacity at first cycle).

(3) Safety performance test of hot box of lithium ion battery

Charging the lithium ion battery to 4.3V at a constant current of 1C at 25 ℃, then charging to a current of less than 0.05C at a constant voltage of 4.3V, and stopping charging; and (3) putting the lithium ion battery in a hot box, heating the lithium ion battery from 25 ℃ to 150 ℃ at a heating rate of 5 ℃/min, keeping the temperature unchanged after the temperature reaches 150 ℃, and then starting timing until the surface of the lithium ion battery starts to smoke.

(4) Low-temperature discharge performance test of lithium ion battery

At 25 ℃, charging the lithium ion battery to 4.3V at a constant current of 1C, then charging the lithium ion battery to a constant voltage of 4.3V until the current is less than 0.05C, then discharging the lithium ion battery to 2.8V at a constant current of 1C, and measuring the discharge capacity of the lithium ion battery and marking as the initial discharge capacity.

Charging the lithium ion battery to 4.3V at a constant current of 1C at 25 ℃, then charging at a constant voltage of 4.3V until the current is less than 0.05C, then placing the lithium ion battery in a low-temperature box at-20 ℃, taking out after placing for 120 minutes, then discharging to 2.8V at a constant current of 1C, and recording the discharge capacity of the lithium ion battery after low-temperature storage.

Capacity ratio (%) after low-temperature discharge of lithium ion battery (discharge capacity after low-temperature storage of lithium ion/initial discharge capacity of lithium ion battery at 25 ℃) x 100%

(5) Nail penetration safety performance test of lithium ion battery

At 25 ℃, the lithium ion battery is charged with a 1C constant current to 4.3V and then with a 4.3V constant voltage to a current of less than 0.05C, at which time the lithium ion battery is in a fully charged state. Nail penetration testing is carried out on the lithium ion battery at the speed of 150mm/s by adopting a nail with the diameter of 3mm, and whether the lithium ion battery smokes, fires or explodes is observed. And if not, determining that the lithium ion battery passes the nail penetration test.

TABLE 3 results of Performance test of examples 1 to 28 and comparative examples 1 to 9

As can be seen from the analysis of the test results in table 2, the electrolytes of the lithium ion batteries in embodiments 1 to 28 include imine-type lithium salts, and the content of the imine-type lithium salts in the electrolytes of the lithium ion batteries in embodiments 1 to 28 is moderate, so that the lithium ion batteries have the advantages of good cycle performance, good rate performance, high safety performance, and good low-temperature discharge performance, and meanwhile, the lithium ion batteries also have the advantage of high energy density by adjusting the group margin of the lithium ion batteries within a proper range.

Comparative examples 1 to 3 use conventional LiPF only6As lithium salt, the lithium ion battery has poor cycle performance, rate capability, safety performance and low-temperature discharge performance.

The elongation at break of the positive electrode current collector of the lithium ion battery of comparative example 4 is too low, which may cause the positive electrode sheet to be broken during the production process, thereby causing the production thereof to be impossible.

The elongation at break of the positive current collector of the lithium ion battery in the comparative example 5 is too high, and although the cycle performance, the rate performance and the low-temperature discharge performance of the lithium ion battery can be improved to a certain extent, the nail penetration rate of the lithium ion battery is reduced due to the too high elongation at break of the positive current collector, so that the lithium ion battery has great potential safety hazard.

The thickness of the positive electrode current collector of the lithium ion battery of comparative example 6 was too small, which also caused the positive electrode sheet to be broken during the production process, thereby causing the production thereof to be impossible.

The thickness of the positive current collector of the lithium ion battery in the comparative example 7 is too large, and although the cycle performance, the rate performance and the low-temperature discharge performance of the lithium ion battery can be improved to a certain extent, the nail penetration rate of the lithium ion battery is reduced due to the too large thickness of the positive current collector, so that the lithium ion battery has great potential safety hazard.

The group margin design of the lithium ion battery of the comparative example 8 is too small, and the 0.5C discharge capacity of the lithium ion battery is low, so that the actual use requirement of the lithium ion battery is difficult to meet.

The group margin of the lithium ion battery of comparative example 9 was over-designed, and although the 0.5C discharge capacity of the lithium ion battery could be improved, the rate capability, low temperature discharge capability and cycle performance of the lithium ion battery were all poor.

Therefore, the present invention is not limited to the specific embodiments disclosed and described above, and some modifications and variations of the present invention should fall within the scope of the claims of the present invention.
